intent: Let zsh users load ripgrep completions with `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`. When the generated rg.zsh is sourced after compinit, it registers `_rg` through `compdef`. It still runs `_rg "$@"` when autoloaded as `_rg` or when compdef is missing (the ci/test-complete harness). The FAQ zsh section gains the missing fpath step and the source-based alternative, with a note on startup cost.

findings.title: Sourcing before compinit runs _rg at top level and errors
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the no-compdef fallback to the test harness, e.g. `if [[ $funcstack[1] == _rg || $_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS == (1|t*|y*) ]]; then _rg "$@"; elif (( $+functions[compdef] )); then compdef _rg rg; fi`. Optionally print a hint in a final else branch. Also say in FAQ.md that the `source` line must come after `compinit`. ci/test-complete sets _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1, so it keeps working.
findings.why_it_matters: The FAQ tells users to add `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` to .zshrc but does not say where. If that line runs before compinit, or when compinit is never run, compdef is undefined. The guard then calls `_rg "$@"` at top level, and every new shell prints `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments`. No completion is registered. This is the same kind of startup error that issue #2956 reported. Keeping the direct-call fallback for the test harness only, and saying 'after compinit' in the FAQ, avoids it.
evidence: FAQ.md:134-136 -- ```zsh / $ source <(rg --generate complete-zsh) / ``` (no placement relative to compinit given)
zsh 5.8.1 scratch run: `zsh -f -c 'source <(cat _rg)'` -> `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments`, rc=1; after `compinit` the same source gives rc=0 and _comps[rg]=_rg
ci/test-complete:17 -- ( _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source $1 ) -- the harness already sets a distinguishing variable

findings.title: FAQ .zshrc snippet includes a literal `$ ` prompt
findings.suggested_fix: Change the line to `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` with no `$ `, matching the prompt-free `fpath=(...)` .zshrc snippet just above. While there, fix 'easier to setup, is generally slower' -> 'easier to set up, it is generally slower'.
findings.why_it_matters: The text says to add this block to .zshrc. A user who pastes it as-is gets `zsh: command not found: $` on every shell start, and completions never load. The fpath snippet three lines above correctly leaves out the prompt, so the two .zshrc snippets are inconsistent.

findings.title: Autoload under a name other than _rg misses the first TAB
findings.suggested_fix: Decide based on how the file is being run, not on the function's name: `[[ $zsh_eval_context[-1] == loadautofunc ]]` is true when the file is autoloaded and false when it is sourced.
findings.why_it_matters: The parent commit completed on the first TAB whatever the file was named. With this change, a copy installed in fpath under another name (e.g. `_ripgrep`) runs `compdef _rg rg` on its first call and offers no completions. Later TABs work because the mapping has moved to `_rg`. All official artifacts (release.yml, ci/build-and-publish-m2, the FAQ) install the file as `_rg`, and the funcstack check is a common idiom, so this is a narrow edge left to the maintainer.
evidence: zsh 5.8.1 scratch run: file autoloaded as _ripgrep with compinit; calling _ripgrep returns 0 without completing and _comps[rg] changes from _ripgrep to _rg
adversarial zpty test: first TAB beeps with no completion under the _ripgrep name; the parent commit completes

actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Limit the no-compdef fallback to the test harness (e.g. also check `$_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS`), and say in FAQ.md that the `source` line must come after `compinit`.

residual_risks: The FAQ does not say that the fpath line must run before compinit. Users who add it after compinit (for example, after oh-my-zsh has already run compinit) get no rg completion until compinit is re-run or a stale .zcompdump is removed. The code path works; only the instructions are unclear. (correctness, adversarial)
testing_gaps: ci/test-complete only covers the no-compdef branch (sourced in a subshell with _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1). Nothing tests the new compdef registration branch (source after compinit) or the autoload-as-_rg branch, so a mistake in the guard would pass CI.
